standard.title: Measurement of Diameter and Girth of Trees — Guidelines
standard.description: This standard specifies guidelines, technical procedures, and operational precautions for standardizing how the diameter and girth of trees should be measured across diverse field conditions in India. It establishes a uniform methodology for forestry measurements to ensure consistency, accuracy, and comparability of ecological data used to estimate forest biomass, assess carbon stocks, and monitor biodiversity.

certification.description: Voluntary Code of Practice. Since IS 19723:2026 is an operational guideline and code of practice for field measurements rather than a physical consumer material, it does not carry an individual mandatory BIS 'ISI Mark' product certification stamp. However, compliance with its measurement protocols, error-minimisation checklists, and rounding norms is universally mandated by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEF&CC), state forest departments, wildlife institutes, and carbon-credit validation boards across India to ensure standardisation, accuracy, and comparability of ecological field data.
requirements: Specifies that the measuring tape must be wrapped perpendicular to the tree's longitudinal axis, leveled around the stem at the Point of Measurement (PoM) ensuring it is not twisted. The reading must be recorded exactly where the tape's zero mark meets the graduated scale.
Diameter measurements must be recorded in centimetres (cm), with its instrument least count considered to be 1 millimetre (1 mm).
Girth measurements must be recorded in centimetres (cm), with its instrument least count considered to be 1 millimetre (1 mm).

Establishes the mathematical relationship:
Girth (G) = π × diameter (D) [where π = 22/7]
Diameter can be calculated from girth:
Diameter (D) = girth (G)/π.
Calculated girth and diameter values must be reported in centimetres (cm) with a minimum of two (2) decimal places.
